method: Every one of the 16 key disagreements was read individually. NOTHING here is
applied by this file; apply-adjudication.ts is a separate, explicit step.
THE ADJUDICATION AXIS IS DERIVABLE-vs-RECALL, NOT PART A vs PART B.
reconcile-key.ts prints the Part A/B split because that is the cheap proxy, but
it is too blunt and the difference showed up on Q69: Part B's Physics and
Chemistry items are as derivable as anything in Part A, and deferring to the key
on one of those would be deferring on a question the page settles. The rule
actually applied:
DERIVABLE (Part A, plus Physics/Chemistry/Biology-fact items in Part B)
-- re-derive from the page and let the derivation win where it is decisive.
RECALL (history, polity, current affairs, and anything turning on an external
fact this pass does not hold) -- the KEY is the stronger source, because a
single blind pass measures ~94% on recall. Defer unless the key is
SELF-REFUTING against the stem's own words.
THE KEY IS THIRD-PARTY, NOT OFFICIAL, and its own heading misnames the exam
('CDS II 2026 - GAT'), which is a carelessness signal but not evidence about any
individual answer. Agreement of 89.3% settles that it IS a key for this paper.
CALIBRATION, measured: HIGH 121/127 (95.3%), MED 12/19 (63.2%), LOW 1/4 (25.0%).
The LOW band landing exactly at chance is the derivation brief's honesty rule
working -- the deriver said it did not hold those facts and it was right to.

keepOurs.why: Complex permanent tissue in plants is xylem AND phloem. Tracheids and vessels are xylem components; sieve tubes and companion cells are phloem components. All four listed cells therefore qualify. The key's 'I and II only' is phloem alone and silently drops xylem, which the question's own option A offers. NCERT Class 9, Tissues.

All three statements are near-verbatim NCERT Class 10 Geography (Agriculture): slash-and-burn IS primitive subsistence farming; it IS called jhumming in the North-Eastern states; and 'when the soil fertility decreases, the farmers shift and clear a fresh patch of land'. The key's 'III only' rejects two sentences the textbook prints.

THE STRONGEST OF THE FIVE. The stem asks which LANDLOCKED states border Madhya Pradesh. MP's five neighbours are Rajasthan, Uttar Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Maharashtra and Gujarat -- and Maharashtra and Gujarat both have a coastline. The key's option A lists all five, i.e. it answers 'which states border MP' and ignores the stem's own qualifier. Option D is the three landlocked ones.

keepOurs.class: RECALL, but the fact is not marginal
keepOurs.why: Exercise DUSTLIK is the India-UZBEKISTAN joint exercise and has been since 2019; the India-UAE exercises are Desert Cyclone and Desert Flag. So statement I as printed is false and statement II (semi-mountainous terrain) is the true one. The key's 'I only' inverts both. This is the one keep-ours that rests on an external fact rather than the page, and it is recorded as such.

keepOurs.class: DERIVABLE, grammar convention -- the least decisive of the five
keepOurs.why: Both printed transformations are the standard textbook forms. 'These grapes taste sour' -> 'These grapes are sour when they are tasted' is the canonical passive for a middle-voice perception verb, and 'Forget the past' -> 'Let the past be forgotten' is the canonical imperative passive. The key's 'Neither' requires both to be wrong. Flagged as the weakest of the five because it turns on which grammar convention the examiner used rather than on a fact.

acceptKey.why: THE KEY IS RIGHT ON THE PHYSICS, and this is why the axis is derivable-vs-recall rather than Part A/B. Over a pulley every point of an inextensible rope shares the same SPEED (a scalar), but the descending and ascending sides accelerate in opposite directions, so the acceleration VECTORS differ. Option B states exactly that contrast, which is plainly what the item is testing. Our deriver named B as its runner-up and named the vector reading as what would make it win.
Our deriver's named runner-up. School colloid tables routinely list foam rubber under 'Foam' rather than distinguishing solid foam, so the examiner counts all four pairs matched.

ACCEPTED BUT CONTESTED, and worth a second eye. The stem scopes itself to 'respiration in ANIMALS', and in animals anaerobic respiration yields lactic acid with no CO2 -- which makes statement III true and our 'I and III' right. The key's 'I only' is the yeast/fermentation reading, which the stem's own scope excludes. Our deriver named this exact tension in advance and called it its least secure item in the range. Deferring on the recall rule, not because the key is clearly right.

Statement II dates the blast furnace to the beginning of the 18th century, which matches the standard narrative of Darby's coke-smelting blast furnace (1709) that Industrial-Revolution chapters teach. Recall item, key defers.
Our deriver's named runner-up, winning exactly on the re-housing it flagged: the fellowship sits under the Research, Development and Innovation Fund. Recall, past our reliable knowledge.
Our deriver's named runner-up, winning exactly on the condition it flagged ('B if Mirage 2000 was dropped'). Recall about one edition's participant list.
The key holds statement I false and II true, the inverse of our reading. Neither is settleable from the page. Recall, key defers.

The only Part A row where the key wins. It turns on whether 'Wait here until I return' -> 'wait here until he returned' must shift 'here' to 'there'. The mechanical textbook rule says it must; retention is also taught where speaker and reporter share a place. Re-deriving does not settle a convention, so the key is the only external signal. Our deriver marking this HIGH was overconfident.
The deriver stated outright that it does not hold IBCA membership as of 2026 and chose France on a range-state pattern argument alone. Key wins; this is what LOW is for.

The deriver stated it holds nothing about the March 2026 uranium agreement -- not the parties, not the figure -- and said India-Australia and India-Canada were both live and inseparable. The key says India-Canada. Key wins.
The deriver stated it holds neither the host States nor the mascot of the inaugural Khelo India Tribal Games, and took all three statements rather than manufacture a falsehood. Key wins.
